statement: On Windows, running `cargo test -p enforcer-install` fails the test *binary launch itself* with 'os error 740: The requested operation requires elevation' — not a real permissions issue, but Windows app-compat heuristics flagging an exe whose name contains 'install' (the compiled test binary is literally `enforcer_install-<hash>.exe`). Setting `__COMPAT_LAYER=RunAsInvoker` in the shell env before running cargo test/clippy resolves it completely; no admin elevation is actually needed.
why: Any worker running tests for a crate named `*install*`/`*setup*`/`*update*` on Windows will hit this and may misdiagnose it as a real permissions/build problem, wasting time trying `Run as Administrator` or CI-runner permission fixes.
howToApply: Before running cargo test/clippy against `enforcer-install` (or any future crate whose name matches Windows UAC installer heuristics) on Windows, export `__COMPAT_LAYER=RunAsInvoker` in the same shell/session first.

evidence.ref: cargo test -p enforcer-install failed with 'os error 740' until __COMPAT_LAYER=RunAsInvoker was exported, then 94/94 lib tests passed

statement: Cargo's `CARGO_BIN_EXE_<name>` env var is ONLY set for a crate's OWN `[[bin]]` targets — it is NOT set for a dev-dependency's binary, even though `enforcer-cli`'s `[[bin]] name = "enforcer"` is a dev-dependency of `enforcer-install` specifically to make the real binary available to tests. Both `env!("CARGO_BIN_EXE_enforcer")` (compile-time, in both src/ unit tests and tests/ integration tests) and `std::env::var("CARGO_BIN_EXE_enforcer")` (runtime) returned NotPresent/compile error. The working pattern: resolve `std::env::current_exe()`, take two `.parent()` calls to get from `<profile>/deps/<test>.exe` to `<profile>/`, then join `enforcer<EXE_SUFFIX>` — since all workspace crates' bin outputs land in the same shared `target/<profile>/` dir.
why: c04's workpack required shelling out to the REAL `enforcer` binary from `enforcer-install`'s tests to prove the seeded-fixture deny/allow/allow-with-warning contract against the actual subprocess (not a simulation). The intuitive/documented `CARGO_BIN_EXE_<name>` approach silently fails for this exact cross-crate-dependency shape, which any future c05/c06+ pack needing the same real-binary-in-tests pattern (e.g. sessionstart hook fixtures) will also hit.
howToApply: For any enforcer-install (or similar) test that needs to invoke the real `enforcer` binary built by `enforcer-cli`, do NOT rely on `env!`/`std::env::var("CARGO_BIN_EXE_enforcer")`. Instead resolve it via `std::env::current_exe()?.parent()?.parent()?.join(format!("enforcer{}", std::env::consts::EXE_SUFFIX))`, and assert `.is_file()` with a clear error pointing at `cargo build -p enforcer-cli` if missing.

evidence.ref: crates/enforcer-install/tests/pretooluse_hook_fixtures.rs enforcer_binary() — env! failed to compile, std::env::var returned NotPresent, current_exe()-relative resolution succeeded and all 3 seeded-fixture tests passed
